changes.text: 要不要修京通铁路，朝中有了争执。《清史稿·张之洞传》记下这场争执只用了一句话：「會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」。海军衙门主张修，台谏争陈铁路之害、请停办——至于害具体是哪几条，主张修的一方又答了什么，传文都没有抄录，只留下一个「請停辦」的收口。

The proposed Beijing-Tongzhou railway drew opposition at court. The Draft History of the Qing takes a single sentence over the dispute (here and throughout, quotations from the Chinese are our own translations): "When the Naval Office petitioned to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, the remonstrating officials pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted." The Naval Office stood for building; the censors and remonstrating officials - the Qing court's remonstrance officials - pressed the harms and asked for a stop. Which harms, and what the other side answered, the biography never copies down. It closes on the bare "asked that the project be halted."
作者的一种读法是，这份议奏包含三个部分：排目标次序（通土货、厚民生最大，征兵转饷次之），列逐条的「利」并编号，落实到官职（北路直隶总督、南路湖广总督、河南巡抚为副）。作者认为，这样写可能把争论从“有没有害”引向“这些逐条的「利」成不成立、这三位督抚之职扛不扛得动”。

One reading is that the memorial has three components: a ranking of goals (moving goods and enriching livelihoods greatest, raising troops and forwarding supplies next); a numbered, item-by-item list of benefits; and responsibility assigned to offices (north to the Governor-General of Zhili, south to the Governor-General of Huguang, the Governor of Henan as deputy). In the author's view, writing it this way may steer the argument away from "is it harmful" toward "do these itemized benefits hold, and can these three offices carry them."
一种解释是，「厚民生」排在「徵兵、轉餉」之前，是把争议最小、也最难被驳倒的目标放在最前面：台谏说的是「鐵路之害」，而避敌、避坟庐这两条或许是对着「害」字去答的（传文未记台谏所指何害）。作者推断这种写法出于策略考虑，传文没有写他的思考过程，此处是作者的解释。

One reading: putting "enriching livelihoods" before "raising troops and forwarding supplies" sets the least contested, hardest-to-topple goal at the front. The censors spoke of "the harms of railways," and the two points about avoiding the enemy and sparing graves and houses may answer the word "harms," though the biography does not record which harms were meant. The author infers that this drafting is tactical; the biography records no thought process, so this is the author's interpretation.
再次，传文没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁或争议后续，本文不替他补写；「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工，更不等于办成。本文也不把原文没有的公元年份换算出来，更不会说他事先知道结果——他写下那些「利」的时候，看到的只是清单，不是成绩单。

Third, the biography records no schedule, outlay, relocations, or aftermath of the dispute for the proposed line, and this article does not fill them in. "Approved by rescript" is approval, not the start of work, still less a finished line. This article also converts no Common Era years the original does not have, and will not say he knew the outcome in advance: when he wrote those numbered benefits, what lay before him was a checklist, not a report card.

dispositions.rationale: 所引原文实为一句（三个分句），将“两句话”改为“一句话”，英文 just two sentences 改为 a single sentence。

evidence.quote: 會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦

dispositions.rationale: 摘录只到「利六」，不能断定总数为六。“这六条”改为“这些逐条的「利」”，英文改为 these itemized benefits，与 story.0 的保留意见一致。

evidence.quote: 太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六

dispositions.rationale: 传文未记台谏所指何害，原文用“恰好”写成了定论。现改为“或许是对着「害」字去答的”，并补注“传文未记台谏所指何害”，英文同步改为 may answer… though the biography does not record which harms were meant。

evidence.quote: 內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二

dispositions.rationale: 同 F2，证据不足以断定「利」只有六条。“那六条「利」”改为“那些「利」”，英文 those six benefits 改为 those numbered benefits。
